definitions.explanation: A helmet, especially the ornate helmets worn by samurai warriors. Also refers to decorative replicas displayed during Boys' Day (端午の節句) and other cultural occasions.

examples.japanese: {武士|ぶし}が{兜|かぶと}をかぶった。
examples.english: The samurai put on his helmet.

examples.japanese: {五月|ごがつ}になると{兜|かぶと}を{飾|かざ}る{家庭|かてい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many households display samurai helmets when May comes around.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}には{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}の{兜|かぶと}や{鎧|よろい}が{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: Helmets and armor from the Warring States period are on display at the museum.

notes:
Samurai helmets are characterized by elaborate crests ({前立|まえだて}) and face guards. Miniature {兜|かぶと} are displayed alongside {鎧|よろい} (armor) and {鯉|こい}のぼり (carp streamers) during {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく} (Boys' Day, May 5th) to wish for boys' healthy growth.

The idiom {兜|かぶと}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ (to take off one's helmet) means to surrender or admit defeat.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{兜|かぶと}をかぶる — to wear a helmet
・{兜|かぶと}を{飾|かざ}る — to display a helmet
・{兜|かぶと}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ — to surrender; to admit defeat
・{鎧兜|よろいかぶと} — armor and helmet
